<!-- Describe binary provenance and redistribution boundaries for the optional Rust tools. -->
# M12 third-party Rust tools

The optional Rust image uses **official upstream binary distributions**, not a
claimed local source build: Rust/rustc 1.90.0, Cargo 1.90.0 and matching
`x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` std from 2025-09-18. URLs and whole-archive SHA-256
are locked in [inputs.json](../../ports/rust/inputs.json). LLVM is embedded in
the upstream compiler driver. The M11 bootstrap supplies its musl libgcc unwinder.
The Rust application linker is the matching upstream LLVM rust-lld. Rust's
self-contained musl CRT/std files come from the matching Rust distribution;
guest C FFI compilation uses the separately source-built M11 GCC/musl sysroot.

Original Rust/Cargo MIT/Apache, COPYRIGHT and third-party notices accompany the tools.
The GCC unwinder's GPLv3 and runtime exception texts are retained under
`/rs/licenses/unwinder`, including in the Rust-only runtime image.
The first-party launcher, image tools and tests are Apache-2.0. Neither the
compiler nor LLVM is linked into the kernel. Upstream source construction and
compiler self-bootstrap remain separate, unverified work; an installed compiler
does not establish either property.

The online Cargo profile includes the Mozilla CA root store converted by curl,
dated 2026-10-20. Its immutable URL and SHA-256 are locked separately from the
compiler in inputs.json. This certificate data is MPL-2.0; the independently
checksum-locked license is installed at `/rs/licenses/certs/MPL-2.0.txt` and the
unmodified bundle retains its original attribution header. Test CA private keys
remain in host build directories. A public-network test may explicitly supply
an additional public PEM trust bundle for its host proxy; that test input is
separate from the standard image's pinned Mozilla store.
